Scope: HUD shutdown paths, single primary-monitor overlay, long-run stability

ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Delegate to Open-JarvisHud.ps1 without stopping or replacing anything.
ConfirmedDefects.Problem: Startup force-terminated JarvisHud.exe and overwrote installed executables with a staged build.

ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Preserved original as .disabled and installed a compatibility launcher that only starts bin/JarvisHud.exe.
ConfirmedDefects.Problem: Entry-point IL enumerated JarvisHud processes and called Kill before checking the singleton mutex.

ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Both delegate to the canonical launcher.
ConfirmedDefects.Problem: Direct RunOverlay calls bypassed the singleton and supervisor entry point.

ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Read-only for running HUD; starts installed build only when explicitly requested while stopped.
ConfirmedDefects.Problem: Default verification stopped the active HUD and copied a staged executable, racing recovery.

ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Clamp native move/resize coordinates before applying them.
ConfirmedDefects.Problem: Dragging could leave the primary monitor until the next periodic correction.
Disconnected recognition state triggered worker restart without consulting server recoverable flag; WMI, process waits and cross-process window operations ran on the WPF UI thread.
ConfirmedDefects.Fix: Require stale-heartbeat recovery flag; serialize background recovery/window maintenance; use asynchronous cross-process window positioning.

HistoricalLimit: The first unexpected exit has no retained caller record. Confirmed code defects are not proof of which caller caused that one historical event.

UserConfirmedEvents.Event: User dragged HUD during initial observation
User tested explicit Quit menu; normal exit code 0

Result.MicObservationNote: Eight connected=false samples were observed, including the deliberate worker interruption. Every one was followed by connected=true at the next sample. No additional worker restart was logged. This does not establish uninterrupted recognition of human speech.
